A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same cropping-versus-dropout study. Their text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices are readable, and retained material can be matched across revisions and renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original contrastive-training experiments, MTEB scores, in-domain classification results and ablations in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: V2 retains these original experiments and adds classification benchmarks, BERT/RoBERTa experiments and further layerwise evaluations.

M1.justification: The two-sentence cropping procedure, dropout pairing, mean pooling, cosine InfoNCE loss and in-batch negatives are retained. BERT/RoBERTa experiments apply the existing procedure; newly disclosed preprocessing details do not establish a method change.

E1.justification: Table 1 expands from 12 tasks across four MTEB modalities to 19 across five. Seven classification tasks add sentiment and intent/domain recognition coverage, including AmazonPolarity, Banking77 and IMDb. The six datasets used for in-domain representation evaluation are retained.

E2.justification: V2 adds dropout-tuned MPNet to Figure 4b's layerwise comparison and includes untreated BERT/RoBERTa controls in new Table S1. The main off-the-shelf comparator membership in Tables 1–2 remains unchanged.

E3.justification: New evaluation settings include train/test logistic regression with 100 maximum iterations, controlled fine-tuning experiments with BERT and RoBERTa, and layerwise MTEB evaluation using unnormalized embeddings. The block average now covers five modalities. Existing MPNet training settings and kNN splits are retained; normalization disclosures alone do not establish rerunning existing experiments.

E4.justification: New Table S1 tests whether augmentation rankings generalize across backbones. Expanded Figure 4 and new Figure S3 examine layerwise quality across augmentations and MTEB modalities. Conversely, v1's explicit projection-head ablation and its finding of no consistent benefit disappear.

E5.justification: Both Table 2 captions retain the same approximate ±1 percentage-point uncertainty based on binomial standard deviation. Neither version reports additional seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: V2 adds classification, backbone and layerwise results. Its 51.8% cropping average versus v1's 48.7% reflects expanded benchmark coverage, not a same-setting gain. Existing Table 1 BGE-base/BGE-large values are exchanged. Pre-fine-tuning whitening accuracy with cosine distance changes from 46.9% to 18.5% in v1 Table S2 versus v2 Table S3, reversing the reported benefit.

T1.justification: The InfoNCE objective and appendix metric formulas remain mathematically unchanged. Neither version provides theoretical results or proofs, and v2's added mechanism discussion is conceptual rather than a formal derivation.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain intact. However, the discussion narrows cropping's superiority from 'all evaluations' in v1 to 'all evaluation modalities' in v2, accommodating the newly reported task-level exceptions while retaining the overall augmentation, rapid-adaptation and late-layer claims.

C2.justification: V1's assertion that the last layer always performs best is qualified by penultimate-layer peaks for dropout and for cropping on STS/classification. V2 discusses objective–evaluation misalignment and adds specific limitations concerning training duration and MTEB training only on ICLR. It also withdraws the caption's claim that whitening improves untuned MPNet.

D1.justification: V2 newly specifies period-based sentence splitting, SentenceTransformers normalization and normalization differences between evaluations, and adds the RoBERTa checkpoint. The removed projection-head report also removes its architecture dimensions. Main hyperparameters, hardware and code-access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Related work substantially expands to distinguish encoder and generative embedding models, instruction tuning and newer contrastive approaches. Added works include E5, GTE, CoCondenser and NV-Embed. Section 4 explicitly positions the layer findings relative to Skean et al. (2025); these additions extend beyond bibliographic updates.

P1.justification: V2 substantially rewrites and reorganizes related work into three subsections, revises the abstract and introductory framing, reworks the layer discussion and introduces a separate Limitations section. Training without pre-training moves from Section 3.3.4 to Section 3.4.

P2.justification: Table 1 gains a classification block, new Table S1 presents backbone comparisons, Figure 4 expands from two to three panels, and Figure S3 is added. Figures 1 and 3 move from text-wrapped placements to standalone displays, while captions and supplementary layouts are revised.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens the evidence behind the broad conclusions by testing additional backbones and a previously omitted task family. Its expanded layer analysis exposes exceptions to final-layer optimality, improving the conclusions' calibration, while clearer limitations and implementation disclosures aid interpretation. Losing the explicit projection-head check and leaving some numerical revisions unexplained are drawbacks, but the broader tests and more qualified conclusions provide a substantial overall gain.
